title: Matched-delivery search bounds exclude feasible curve patterns
acceptance:
## Problem and Evidence
The phase-two matched-delivery study uses a reference-centered face-angle search box. For pitching wedge, zero lean and doubled curve, the strong-draw box is [0, 6] degrees and excludes the actual conditional-model raw-landing solution at face -0.26045964 degrees, path +2.73954036 degrees, speed 32.04591426 m/s. Fade is the mirror. A symmetric [-6,+6] face box with unchanged [24,40] m/s speed bounds matches the same 77.40247725 m target; nominal residual is 1.14e-13 m and finer replay residual is 0.0002114 m. The 0.05 m acceptance tolerance is unchanged. This is a search-bound artifact, not physical impossibility or empirical validation.

Evidence: docs/research/shot_pattern_analysis/phase2/review_followups/WEDGE_MATCH_BOUNDS_REVIEW.md and its reproducible probe/receipt. The original 324-cell primary and 72-cell control runs must remain immutable and separately labeled.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Preserve current frozen workers, parameters, acceptance receipt and historical unavailable cells; do not restart or rewrite them.
- Predeclare a supplemental matched analysis with a symmetric absolute face box, unchanged speed bounds, numerical physics settings and matching tolerance.
- Cover the 18 omitted PW zero-lean doubled-curve cells (both shaft SDs, all nine noise profiles), 10,000 attempts per pattern. Diagnose control bounded failures separately; include additional face-bound artifacts only with recorded evidence and explicit plan.
- Implement explicit configurable nominal bounds using TDD, design-by-contract, existing numerical/data APIs, and no duplicated simulation loop. Validate default behavior and provenance. Do not modify accepted sources while the current runs are live.
- Review the source transition, run/audit supplemental outputs, and add clearly labeled curve-strength/lean comparisons and scoring to the report and shareable figures.
- Keep infeasible-search, unsupported-model and physically impossible claims distinct. Do not close before merged implementation/evidence; no empirical accuracy claim.

## Handoff
Active work is on codex/shot-pattern-matched-delivery; final numerical jobs are running under the prior immutable execution acceptance. Supplemental execution waits for those jobs and a reviewed implementation/plan. Related publication audit issue #11988 and report issue #11976.


## Reviewed Supplemental Protocols
Further deterministic probes show that the 5°-lean wedge strong curves also match under the symmetric face box: face ±0.076707602°, speed 29.161308145 m/s, and fine-replay residual 0.000289371 m. The 5°-lean driver strong curves need 56.345074274 m/s, just 0.095074274 m/s above the original 56.25 m/s ceiling; face is ±4.894851870° and fine-replay residual is 0.000943089 m. These are conditional-model nominal solutions, not empirical measurements.

The supplement has 26 distinct Monte Carlo cells:

| Group | Cells | Scope | Face Bounds | Speed Factors |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| A | 18 | Wedge, 0° lean, doubled curve; both shaft SDs and all nine profiles | −6° to +6° | 0.75–1.25 |
| B | 4 | Wedge, 5° lean, fixed target; both SDs, shaft-only and combined-2 profiles | −6° to +6° | 0.75–1.25 |
| C | 4 | Driver, 5° lean, fixed target; both SDs, shaft-only and combined-2 profiles | −6° to +6° | 0.75–1.30 |

Group C is a separately labeled speed-bounds sensitivity study. Four wedge 0°-lean control records explicitly reference the equivalent Group A data with provenance, rather than claiming new runs. Every group retains 10,000 attempts per pattern, the 0.05 m matching tolerance, and the physical/numerical settings. The plan was adapted after a feasibility audit and declared before supplemental Monte Carlo; it is not the original protocol. The existing 324/72-cell records remain immutable.

Final reporting must distinguish original bounded-search status from supplemental resolved status and identify the source/protocol for every comparison. Do not silently replace historical data or claim global physical impossibility. Root approved the separate speed extension only after the nominal probe; this supersedes the earlier instruction to retain speed bounds for every group. Groups A and B still retain the original speed limits.

Exact inventory and review: `docs/research/shot_pattern_analysis/phase2/review_followups/SUPPLEMENTAL_EXECUTION_INVENTORY.json` and `SUPPLEMENTAL_BOUNDS_PLAN.md`, committed in `55c2f26101`.


## Integration Review Findings
The first implementation review found two additional acceptance requirements:

- GUI configuration import must preserve and visibly identify explicit face bounds and speed factors. Loading a supplemental request and then exporting or running it currently drops those fields back to defaults. Add a failing round-trip test, fix the controls/state, and retain legacy configuration defaults.
- Final supplemental execution acceptance must bind the reviewed protocol and exact cell/configuration inventory, in addition to source hashes and evidence files. A receipt for one reviewed group must not authorize a different unreviewed group merely because the software source is identical. Add rejection tests for mismatched protocol, selection and bounds; retain the original matrix acceptance behavior.

Both findings are being fixed in the isolated bounds worktree before integration or supplemental Monte Carlo. Original frozen workers are unchanged. A separate interpretation review also found that mirrored zero-error draw/fade nominals do not imply equal stochastic outcomes: shaft twist couples face angle and loft, so the full joint delivery distribution need not be reflection-symmetric even with diagonal primitive noise. Report measured simulation differences without imposing that symmetry.
